/-!
# Erdős Problem 113

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/113](https://www.erdosproblems.com/113)
- [ErSi84] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Cube-supersaturated graphs and related problems*.
  Progress in graph theory (Waterloo, Ont., 1982) (1984), 203-218.
- [Er90] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990),
  467-478.
- [Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991),
  397-406.
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [Ja23b] Janzer, Oliver, *Disproof of a conjecture of Erdős and Simonovits on the Turán number
  of graphs with minimum degree 3*. Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN (2023), 8478--8494.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Asymptotics SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos113

/--
If $G$ is bipartite then $\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\ll n^{3/2}$ if and only $G$ is $2$-degenerate, that
is, $G$ contains no induced subgraph with minimal degree at least 3.

Conjectured by Erdős and Simonovits [ErSi84]. Erdős first offered \$250 for a proof and \$100 for
a counterexample, but in [Er93] offered \$500 for a counterexample. Disproved by Janzer [Ja23b]
who constructed, for any $\epsilon>0$, a $3$-regular bipartite graph $H$ such that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;H)\ll n^{\frac{4}{3}+\epsilon}.$$

See also [146](https://www.erdosproblems.com/146) and [147](https://www.erdosproblems.com/147).

The linked formal proof refutes the "only if" direction via Janzer's construction.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos113.lean#L4902"]
theorem erdos_113 : answer(False) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsBipartite →
    (((fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n G : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)) ↔
      G.IsDegenerate 2) := by
  sorry

end Erdos113

findings.description: The docstring's attribution “Conjectured by Erdős and Simonovits [ErSi84]” points to the wrong paper for this conjecture. The cited Cube-supersaturated graphs and related problems discusses supersaturation conjectures, not the asserted characterization by 2-degeneracy. The Lean statement itself is faithful to the conjecture stated in Janzer's paper.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Simonovits, Cube-supersaturated graphs and related problems (1984), pp. 205–206, states conjectures about numbers of copies in supersaturated graphs (https://renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1984-04.pdf). Janzer, arXiv:2109.06110v2, Conjecture 1.3 states exactly: “Let H be a bipartite graph. Then ex(n,H)=O(n^{3/2}) holds if and only if H is 2-degenerate.” Its introduction and bibliography instead identify earlier Erdős sources, including Problems and results in graph theory (1981); the corresponding degree conjectures appear on p. 335 of https://renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-20.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the attribution with “Conjectured by Erdős and Simonovits (see [Ja23b, Conjecture 1.3] and the historical references there).” No change to the Lean theorem is needed.

reformulations.difference: IsDegenerate 2 quantifies over nonempty finite vertex sets and counts neighbors within each set, whereas Janzer defines degeneracy using minimum degrees of subgraphs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a finite graph, every vertex subset is represented by a Finset, and neighborsWithin counts precisely the degree in its induced subgraph. An arbitrary subgraph on that vertex set has no larger degrees, while induced subgraphs are themselves subgraphs. Thus the two degeneracy conditions are equivalent. The scratch file also proves the finite-set no-3-core characterization and equivalence with the linked proof's Set/ncard definition; the full arbitrary-subgraph bridge was not separately formalized.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization found. Checked quantifier scope, graph-dependent asymptotic constants, ordinary rather than induced containment in extremalNumber, real division in the exponent, and the polarity of answer(False). Scratch proofs cover n = 0, empty and edgeless forbidden graphs, and a non-2-degenerate K₃,₃. Rebuilt all 45 modules of the pinned external proof and proved the exact reviewed statement from it in /workspace/review/proofcheck.lean; both axiom checks returned only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The target file remains byte-for-byte identical to the committed file. The Erdős Problems webpage returned a Cloudflare challenge, and full texts of the later historical surveys were unavailable; the mathematical claim and its negative resolution were checked directly against Janzer's cited primary paper.
